faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: Can I create a bible meeting anywhere in the world?
faq.a1: Yes, Christianitatis encourages the creation of home churches anywhere there are people willing to worship.
faq.q2: When I register a Home Church, is my personal data available to anyone who visits the site?
faq.a2: We do not expose your sensitive data publicly. The site only shows essential information such as neighborhood and time, and direct contact is protected or made through the platform.
faq.q3: Do I need to log in to access the host's contact for each Home Church?
faq.a3: Yes, to ensure community safety, access to host contact details requires authentication.
faq.q4: How long does a bible meeting last?
faq.a4: The time may vary according to each group, but generally meetings last between 1.5 to 2 hours.
faq.a5: The forum is open to all registered members on the platform who wish to discuss biblical topics and share experiences.
faq.q6: Do I need to be a Christian to participate in any Home Church?
faq.a6: No, everyone is welcome to participate, listen to the word, and learn more about the Christian faith, regardless of their current belief.

aboutUs.title: Our Mission
aboutUs.missionDescription: Christianitatis' mission is to teach people to start Home Churches worldwide as a dynamic and multipliable structure, capable of expanding continuously as long as essential conditions are maintained. We believe that the quality of leadership and the vitality of spiritual life are indispensable foundations for the flourishing and sustainability of these faith communities.

startMeeting.title: Home Church
startMeeting.whatIsChurchDesc: The Church is us, gathered and reconciled with God through Jesus Christ. The Church is a collective spiritual reality formed by people who unite and relate because they have been saved, born again, and received eternal life by grace, through faith in Jesus Christ. Under the leadership and authority of Jesus Christ, the Church, in unity, is called to proclaim the gospel and manifest the love and Kingdom of God on Earth.
startMeeting.whatIsHomeChurchDesc:
Because it is not a religious institution, a building, or a hierarchical structure, that is, because it is not an organization but an organism, the Church can express itself and gather anywhere, especially in a home, as a community of people who share the same faith and meet to worship God, learn from the Word, and live in love and fellowship with one another.

The first worship of Jesus Christ occurred in a house, in a home (Matthew 2:11). Several of Jesus' healings, preachings, and even the Last Supper took place in homes (Matthew 8:14-16; Matthew 26:18; Mark 2:1). The apostle Paul also sends greetings to several churches in homes, as we can see in Romans 16:3-5, 1 Corinthians 16:19, and Philemon 1:2. Even before his death, Paul gathered the Church at home (Acts 28:30-31).

The home church represents a way to establish and re-establish fellowship with one another.
